touches.text: Every device has a shim. Each shim is its own process, one per instance, and connects to the bus as a client (agreed 2026-10-26).
The shim always starts its device. Nothing else does.
It wakes the device when it's not running and is needed.

If the device won't come up, the shim retries; after many retries it files a trouble ticket for Akien and CC to check. This holds for every wake: a request, a pulse, the sleep token (eg the web server failing to come up).
It answers what it can itself; when it can't (eg a health question it holds no answer to), it wakes the device and asks.

A device may declare an idle time; the shim stops it after that long unused, and the next message wakes it again (5.2.6). With none declared it runs until `stop`. Idle costs memory, not CPU, so eg the librarian, slow to load, stays warm for hours, while something cheap can stop after a minute. (Q#19, Akien 2026-11-04)
Processes all messages from the bus for its device.
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

Processes the sleep cycle, if its device needs one: when the sleep token arrives, it wakes its device to do its sleep (the device does the sleeping, not the shim), then passes the token on. If its device won't come up, the shim files the trouble and still passes the token on, so the rest of the rack sleeps.
Writes its runtime data, if any, to ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/
Three kinds of device sit behind a shim:
The shims handle all interfacing with the outside world (ruling 2026-09-11): a device that needs to speak a foreign protocol (eg OpenAI's wire format) does it in its shim.
COMMANDS: The Device commands. The shim answers start and stop itself.

A bare `cairn librarian` never prints URLs. It (1) launches the librarian's shim, which (2) parses the request (nothing) and so (3) launches the librarian and (4) launches a browser pointed at the librarian's chat page. That http request arrives at the web server's shim, which launches the web server, which then displays the librarian's page with focus on the chat window. Each part is self-initializing (Q#30, Akien 2026-11-06).
One web server. A device gets a PANE in it, never a server of its own.
